title: {{Rose}}'s kitchen table
situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Rose}} has gone out. On her kitchen table lies a magazine open to an advertisement, and the television can show the news.

media.title: Century: World War Three
facts: Analysts weigh an Arctic war fought largely by androids: American marine combat units against Russian cold-weather machines; the UN calls it a war everybody would lose.

media.title: a {{CyberLife}} advertisement
facts: The advertisement sells your own model as the number one android for home assistance, starting at 899 dollars.

media.title: the national news
facts: The country is in shock after androids seized a broadcast tower and demanded equal rights; nobody knows whether it is a malfunction or an organized movement, and {{CyberLife}} refuses to comment.

adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

title: The police at {{Rose}}'s door
situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Rose}}, a farmer who smuggles androids across the border, has taken you, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} in; two other fugitive androids are also hiding in her laundry room. {{Rose}} has gone out. A police car has pulled up; an officer is walking to the door. You have about a minute. Around the house are things that would give you away: pouches of blue blood on the kitchen table, an android magazine, {{Luther}} in plain sight, the laundry door open, and the washing machine still running with android uniforms inside.

options.text: Hide everything, get {{Luther}} and {{Alice}} out of sight, shut the laundry door, then answer calmly as the house-sitter.
Hide nothing and just answer the door.

adaptationNote: If evidence is found, the officer discovers the fugitives and {{Luther}} dies stopping him. The dialogue itself does not branch in the game.
